title: Erdos #1158: Hypergraph Turan Lower Bound for K_t(r)

problemStatement.formal: Prove ex_t(n, K_t(r)) >= n^{t - r^{1-t} - o(1)} for complete t-partite t-uniform hypergraphs K_t(r).
problemStatement.plain: Does the expected Erdos lower-bound exponent for complete multipartite t-uniform hypergraph Turan numbers always hold?
whyMatters: Generalizes the Zarankiewicz problem from graphs to t-uniform hypergraphs.
Asks whether the known upper-bound exponent is sharp rather than only probabilistically approximable with a worse constant.
The graph cases t=2, r=2 and r=3 are known, while r >= 4 and higher uniformities remain hard.

proven: Lean defines UniformHypergraph, K_t(r) containment, K_t(r)-freeness, exHypergraph, hypergraphExponent, and the epsilon-form of the conjecture.
The exponent specializes to the graph value 2 - 1/r and the cases r=2,3 compute to 3/2 and 5/3.
Structural bounds show the exponent lies below t, at least t-1, and positive in the stated parameter range.
open: The general lower-bound conjecture is open.
The known t=2, r=2 and t=2, r=3 cases are represented as axioms.
The Erdos upper bound, weaker lower bound, and stepping-up lemma are comments only, not active Lean declarations.
knownResults.goal: Keep the formal hypergraph/Turan scaffold and exponent algebra visible while avoiding claims that the general conjecture or documented bounds are proved in Lean.

currentState.focus: Metadata now emphasizes the formal hypergraph scaffold, exponent algebra, and two axiomatized graph cases instead of implying broader bounds are formal theorems.
blockers: General K_t(r) lower bounds are open.
Only t=2, r=2 and t=2, r=3 known cases are axiomatized.
Upper/lower-bound and stepping-up results are documentation-only in this file.
currentState.nextAction: A next proof slice would strengthen the exHypergraph infrastructure or add verified finite/graph special cases without claiming the full conjecture.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: 5A appropriate (all known results from extremal combinatorics — KST generalization, projective planes, Brown/ERS, stepping-up), 7T proved, 0S.

Stepping-up lemma compounds the constant gap across uniformities
Only algebraic constructions (not probabilistic) achieve tight graph bounds
